elements.title: INTERPRETING THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE SAMPLE CORRELATION COEFFICIENT

nodes: If r is significant and the scatterplot shows a linear trend, the line can be used to predict the value of y for values of x that are within the domain of observed x-values.
If r is not significant OR if the scatterplot does not show a linear trend, the line should not be used for prediction.
If r is significant and the scatterplot shows a linear trend, the line may not be appropriate or reliable for prediction outside the domain of observed x-values in the data.
connections: 1 is a positive condition for using the line for prediction within domain.
2 is a negative condition for using the line for prediction.
3 is a caution about using the line for prediction outside domain.

elements.summary: This diagram explains the conditions under which the sample correlation coefficient r is significant and how that affects the use of a regression line for prediction within or outside the observed data domain.
